quarterly_data.signal: Updated 2026 end-market view: server-related wafer area consumption is now expected to increase by around 46% year-on-year, up from the 44% assumed in the Q1 outlook, supported by strong demand for AI applications, advanced logic and high-bandwidth memory.
quarterly_data.figure: server wafer area consumption +46% YoY in 2026 (Q1 outlook: +44%)

quarterly_data.signal: Memory capacity and allocation continue to prioritise AI-related applications, so less supply is available for other end markets, which is weighing on smartphones and PCs.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Inventories at chip manufacturers in memory and logic had largely normalised, and Siltronic now sees indications that memory players are starting to rebuild wafer safety stocks, most likely to secure supply in an environment of strong AI-driven demand and tightening wafer availability; management called this safety-stock rebuilding a potential additional upside to wafer demand.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Michael Heckmeier: customers are approaching Siltronic to manifest and confirm midterm demand, particularly in the memory space, where customers want to talk about volume developments two to three years out and discussions about new long-term agreements are starting; Siltronic engages but repeats that prices must come up to justify further investment.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: 300-millimeter demand recovery is becoming increasingly evident: new and smaller customers are approaching Siltronic and some existing customers are looking for upside volumes above their long-term agreement levels, which helped drive the Q2 sales improvement and the raised full-year sales guidance; management says it stays very careful and selective about whom it gives which volumes because the price level is still too low.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 sales increased 4.9% quarter-over-quarter to EUR 322 million from EUR 307 million in Q1, driven by higher wafer areas sold, while pricing, product mix and FX remained broadly stable versus the previous quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: sales EUR 322 million, +4.9% QoQ (Q1 2026: EUR 307 million)

quarterly_data.signal: EBITDA rose to EUR 69 million from EUR 65 million in Q1 and the EBITDA margin improved to 21.6% from 21.2%; EBIT remained broadly stable at minus EUR 52 million as higher depreciation largely offset the EBITDA improvement, and the net loss narrowed to EUR 63 million from EUR 67 million.
quarterly_data.figure: EBITDA EUR 69 million, margin 21.6% (Q1: EUR 65 million / 21.2%); EBIT minus EUR 52 million; net loss EUR 63 million (Q1: EUR 67 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Gross profit improved from negative EUR 26 million to negative EUR 14 million as higher wafer areas sold lifted utilisation and fixed-cost absorption; this was partly offset by hedging valuation effects, with the combined FX and hedging result swinging from positive EUR 11 million in Q1 to negative EUR 3 million in Q2 on easing energy and raw-material markets.
quarterly_data.figure: gross profit minus EUR 14 million (Q1: minus EUR 26 million); FX and hedging result minus EUR 3 million (Q1: positive EUR 11 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex amounted to EUR 39 million in Q2 and continues to focus predominantly on 300-millimeter activities; net cash flow improved sequentially but remained negative at EUR 27 million, reflecting continued cash outflow for investments.
quarterly_data.figure: capex EUR 39 million; net cash flow minus EUR 27 million

quarterly_data.signal: Siltronic completed an accelerated bookbuild in June, raising gross proceeds of EUR 273 million by placing new shares equal to 10% of existing share capital at EUR 91 per share, a discount of around 7% to the previous close; the offering was multiple times oversubscribed. Management called it opportunistic and explicitly not tied to a near-term funding need or to a specific capex or deleveraging plan.
quarterly_data.figure: EUR 273 million gross proceeds; 10% of share capital at EUR 91 per share (around 7% discount)

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet at end-June: total assets EUR 4.9 billion versus EUR 4.8 billion at year-end 2025, fixed assets down EUR 93 million as depreciation exceeded capex, cash and securities up to EUR 650 million on the capital increase, equity EUR 2.2 billion for an equity ratio of 45% versus 43% at year-end 2025, net financial debt down to EUR 692 million, plus an undrawn syndicated loan facility of EUR 127 million. Inventories rose on a targeted build to support improving demand and prepare for higher shipment volumes.
quarterly_data.figure: total assets EUR 4.9 billion; cash and securities EUR 650 million; equity EUR 2.2 billion; equity ratio 45%; net financial debt EUR 692 million; undrawn facility EUR 127 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance edged up on the improving demand environment: sales now expected to come in low to mid single digit below 2025, or on/slightly above the prior-year level on a like-for-like basis excluding FX and the closure of the small-diameter business, with wafer areas sold rising year-on-year. EBITDA margin guidance unchanged at 20%-24%, as the better sales outlook is partly offset by higher freight and energy costs than originally assumed. FX assumption: EUR/USD averaged 1.13 in FY2025 versus 1.17 in H1 2026, with 1.18 assumed for H2.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 sales low to mid single digit below 2025 (like-for-like on or slightly above); EBITDA margin 20%-24%; EUR/USD 1.18 assumed for H2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: FabNext Singapore ramp is progressing: as loading increases the fixed-cost burn from the expanded capacity is gradually declining, and CFO Claudia Schmitt confirmed the fab's EBITDA margin will approach group margin level by the end of the year, so the dilution effect fades out. Epitaxy was brought into Singapore, and 200-millimeter for the first time; customer and project qualifications are progressing.
quarterly_data.figure: FabNext EBITDA margin to approach group margin level by end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Utilisation is strong, particularly in the legacy fabs, and overall industry utilisation looks very high; equipment is still flowing into FabNext so capacity and output are still growing there, which is also why capex still runs ahead of the cash number. Lead times for further brownfield equipment are 18-24 months and Siltronic is in close contact with its major suppliers but has not triggered any future capex; no new greenfield fab will be announced anytime soon.
quarterly_data.figure: brownfield equipment lead time 18-24 months

quarterly_data.signal: 300-millimeter pricing: positive price developments are visible on low volumes in the non-LTA space, but spot pricing is still below the LTA price level and clearly below the reinvest level. CEO Michael Heckmeier: 'We always said prices need to come up and to cross the reinvest level. That holds true unchangeably.' Siltronic still expects an overall negative price impact for 2026 and will not commit to further brownfield investment or new long-term agreements until prices cross the reinvest level.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Around two-thirds of Siltronic's business is under long-term agreements, the majority of that in 300-millimeter, with one-third outside LTAs. Management sees no LTA cliff or major LTA change in 2027 or 2028; the major LTAs signed around 2020-2021 to underwrite FabNext run far beyond three years and some run until 2030, while a portfolio of shorter one-to-three-year agreements rolls over and could be renegotiated under better commercial terms in 2027 and 2028 if pricing improves.
quarterly_data.figure: around two-thirds of business under LTAs (majority 300mm); some LTAs run until 2030; no LTA cliff in 2027 or 2028

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 wafer area consumption is still expected to grow by around 7% before inventory effects, unchanged from the Q1 view, but the mix outside servers weakened: smartphones now seen down around 11% and PCs down around 10%, automotive broadly unchanged at moderate growth of around 3%, and industrial applications up around 13% from a relatively low base including demand from data-center infrastructure.
quarterly_data.figure: wafer area consumption +7% in 2026; smartphones -11%; PCs -10%; automotive +3%; industrial +13%

quarterly_data.signal: On the wafer supply-demand balance, CEO Michael Heckmeier said there still seems to be a bit more wafer supply than demand, but that this could change pretty soon in the next quarters, with the price pattern the true indicator; a broad, meaningful wafer price increase has not happened yet, only small volumes here and there, and he argued a very significant price increase must come to the wafer industry to rebalance value creation across the chain.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: 200-millimeter was still sluggish in H1 with prices declining, but a clear volume improvement is expected in H2, driven by power chip manufacturers whose business increasingly benefits from data center, power supply and power management demand; utilisation is rising but is still below 2022 levels, product mix remains negative because the higher-margin float-zone and highly-doped products (MOSFET/IGBT related) are still in low demand, and power-related inventories at customers are improving but remain elevated. Prices are expected to stabilise in H2 from a very low base before the segment contributes meaningfully to revenue or the bottom line.
quarterly_data.figure: 200mm utilisation still below 2022 levels; 200mm prices to stabilise in H2 2026 from a low base

quarterly_data.signal: Recent news flow from a competitor could create another smaller shortage in certain 200-millimeter products; some customers have approached Siltronic to fill that demand and some have even started discussions about 200-millimeter long-term agreements. Siltronic receives 200-millimeter requests from all over the globe including China, where customers want advanced specifications from the established supply base. Siltronic is restaffing lines it had been running on a cost- and cash-optimised basis to follow the demand.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Order visibility: a significant part of Q3 is already negotiated and in the process of being manufactured and shipped, while Q4 is a more mixed picture with some volumes fixed and some still flexible; management expects steady, gradual growth over the remaining quarters rather than a hockey stick. Siltronic rescheduled publication of its Q3 2026 results to November 4, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 results moved to November 4, 2026
